query: What signals suggest an incident will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorising incidents (vpn, network, database, email) gives a real axis to compare resolution times across incident types. Values are well-grounded in short_description text (e.g. 'VPN connection issue' -> vpn, 'Cannot connect to database' -> database). Somewhat overlaps with existing 'category' column but adds finer granularity from free text.

per_column.name: problem_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Symptom type (outage vs cannot_connect vs crash) is a strong signal for resolution difficulty and a genuine new grouping axis. Mostly well-read from text, though mapping 'Email system not working properly' to 'outage' is a mild inference; still defensible. Extraction is a sound reading overall.

per_column.name: is_unassigned_at_open
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident was unassigned at open is a plausible and relevant predictor of longer resolution. However the samples do not show opened-time assignment state, and 'assigned_to' reflects current assignment, not assignment at open time; deriving the 'at_open' temporal claim is only partially supported by the available fields.

per_column.name: assignee_resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Comparing assigned_to vs closed_by is a reasonable proxy for reassignment/handoff, which correlates with longer resolution. Derivable directly from original columns; NULLs handled sensibly for open/unresolved rows. Genuinely useful new axis.

per_column.name: opened_hour_of_day
per_column.rationale: Business_hours vs off_hours is a meaningful signal for resolution latency (staffing). Derivable from opened_at. Grounding is only partially checkable here because the samples expose sys_updated_on/closed_at rather than opened_at, but the bucketing concept is sound and warranted.

per_column.name: is_recurring_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Value is 'true' for 462/500 rows, making it near-constant and offering little analytical leverage. Grounding is weak: recurrence requires cross-row frequency analysis, yet every sampled row is flagged True with no evident support in its source text, suggesting an unsupported blanket assignment.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine, distinct axes (category, symptom type, resolver mismatch, opened-hour bucket, unassigned-at-open) directly relevant to predicting longer resolution, and are largely grounded in the source text or original columns. The main weaknesses are is_recurring_issue_type, which is near-constant and appears unsupported per row, and the 'at_open' temporal columns whose grounding is only partially verifiable from current fields. Overall the set is useful and mostly well-grounded with one weak column.
